questions.stem: You want a **timed** test that keeps every answer hidden until you tap _Finish_. Which mode do you pick?

choices.text: Practice mode
Exam mode
Browse mode (opened from Search or Library)
Due for review
Mistakes

explanation.text: Two ways to answer
Both modes use the same questions. The only real difference is ==when you see the answer==.

explanation.title: Use both
explanation.text: Learn a chapter in **Practice**, then check yourself with an **Exam** a few days later.
To change the time per question: _Settings_ -> _Study_ -> **Exam seconds per question**.

choiceNotes.a: Practice shows the answer and the explanation **right after each tap**. Great for learning, not for testing.
choiceNotes.b: Exam mode is timed and keeps answers hidden until you finish the set.
choiceNotes.c: Browse mode opens a question with the answer **already shown**.
choiceNotes.d: _Due for review_ starts a practice set of the questions your review schedule says are due.
choiceNotes.e: _Mistakes_ starts a practice set of questions you answered wrong before.

questions.stem: You highlight a key line in an explanation. **Where** is that highlight saved?

choices.text: In your Google or Apple account, synced to the cloud
On the app's server, so it follows you everywhere
Nowhere: highlights vanish when you close the app
On this device only, in the app's own storage
Inside the question file that came with the app

explanation.text: Your marks stay with you
Highlights, notes, ink and voice notes are saved in the browser's ==on-device storage== (`IndexedDB`). Nothing is uploaded, and there is no account to create.

items: Each highlight is saved with the **question ID**, which never changes.
the block it belongs to: the question, a choice, or one explanation block
the exact words you marked
a few words before and after, as a backup clue
And its **color**: yellow, green, blue or pink.

explanation.title: Anchored to words, not pixels
explanation.text: Highlights stay in place after rotation, a bigger font or an app update. If an updated question no longer has your words, the app lists those highlights for you instead of dropping them.

explanation.title: One device only
explanation.text: Clearing the browser's site data or removing the app also removes your marks. Export a backup first: _Settings_ -> _Data_.

choiceNotes.a: The app has **no accounts** and no cloud sync.
choiceNotes.b: There is **no server**. The app is a set of files that runs on your device.
choiceNotes.c: Highlights save **instantly** and stay until you remove them.
choiceNotes.d: Everything you add stays on this device, and only you can see it.
choiceNotes.e: Question files are read-only and get replaced by updates. Your marks are kept apart, so updates never touch them.

questions.stem: You are moving to a **new phone**. How do you bring your progress, notes and highlights with you?

choices.text: Export a backup file, then import it on the new phone
Sign in with the same account on the new phone
Just install the app again; progress syncs by itself
Take screenshots of your statistics
Copy the app's question files to the new phone

explanation.text: Move in four steps

items: Old phone: _Settings_ -> _Data_ -> **Export backup**.
Choose **with media** to include voice notes, or without to keep the file small.
Send the file to yourself (AirDrop, email or a cloud drive).
New phone: _Settings_ -> _Data_ -> **Import**, then pick the file.

steps.label: opens
steps.text: The app checks the file and shows what is inside

branches.label: Merge
branches.text: Keeps both: for each item, the newer copy wins

branches.label: Replace
branches.text: Clears this device first, then restores the file

explanation.title: Replace means replace
explanation.text: _Replace_ wipes everything on this device before restoring, so the app asks you to confirm. When unsure, pick **Merge**.
The file is named like `cardiac-mcq-backup-2026-10-26.json`. It works across devices too: iPad <-> phone, Android <-> iPhone.

choiceNotes.a: One file carries everything, and it never leaves your hands.
choiceNotes.b: There are no accounts. That is part of what keeps your data private.
choiceNotes.c: Nothing syncs on its own. A fresh install starts empty.
choiceNotes.d: Screenshots can't be imported. A backup file restores everything.
choiceNotes.e: Question files come with every install. Your **progress** lives elsewhere, and the backup is how you move it.

questions.stem: A banner says **Update available** and you tap _Update_. What happens to your notes, highlights and scores?

choices.text: They are reset, so the new version starts clean
They are kept only if you exported a backup first
They are all kept; only the app's own files are replaced
They move to the cloud during the update

explanation.text: Updates are safe
User progress must survive updates. Never clear or overwrite progress storage when the service worker or cache changes.

explanation.caption: What an update touches
head: Part
Stored in
On update
rows: Replaced with new and fixed questions
Your progress, notes, highlights, ink and voice notes

explanation.title: No rush
explanation.text: _Update_ => the app reloads with the new version. _Later_ => keep studying; the update waits for you.
The app checks for a new version each time you open it while online. Offline, it simply runs the version you have.

choiceNotes.a: Updates never clear your data. That is a firm rule of this app.
choiceNotes.b: A backup is always wise, but an update does not need one.
choiceNotes.c: The app's files and your data are stored apart, so an update only swaps the app's files.
choiceNotes.d: Nothing goes to the cloud, ever.

questions.stem: You answer a question **correctly** for the 1^st^ time. When will spaced repetition bring it back for review?

choices.text: In 10 minutes
In 1 day
In 3 days
In about a week
Never; correct answers are done

explanation.text: Gaps that grow
Each answer moves the question's next review date. Right answers ↑ the gap; a wrong answer ↓ it to minutes. ==You never grade yourself==: the app uses whether you were right and how long you took.

explanation.title: Example with the starting ease of 2.5

steps.label: wrong
steps.text: **10 minutes**, then the gaps start again

items: Fast and right (under 20 s): ease **+0.05**, up to 3.0
Slow and right (over 90 s): ease **−0.05**
Wrong: ease **−0.2**, never below 1.3

explanation.title: Two minutes a day
explanation.text: Tap **Due for review** on Home once a day. It is the fastest way to keep what you learned.

choiceNotes.a: 10 minutes is for a **wrong** answer, so you see it again while it is fresh.
choiceNotes.b: The 1^st^ correct answer schedules the next review 1 day later.
choiceNotes.c: 3 days comes after the 2^nd^ correct answer in a row.
choiceNotes.d: Longer gaps come later: from the 3^rd^ correct answer on, the gap grows by the question's _ease_.
choiceNotes.e: Every question keeps coming back, with longer and longer gaps.

questions.stem: You draw an arrow on an explanation table with Apple Pencil, then **rotate** your iPad. Where is the arrow now?

choices.text: Gone: ink is cleared when the screen size changes
At the same spot on the screen, so it may now cover other text
Moved to the scratchpad
Saved as a picture in your photo library
On the same spot of the table, resized to fit

explanation.text: Ink that sticks to the content

Every explanation block has its own clear drawing layer. Each point of a stroke is saved as x~1~, y~1~, p~1~: the position as a **fraction** of the block's size, plus pen pressure. So `x = 0.5` means the middle of the block on any screen.

explanation.title: Rest your hand
explanation.text: Once the app sees your Apple Pencil, finger touches **scroll** instead of drawing. Two fingers always scroll.
Turn drawing on with the **Draw** button (or press `D` on a keyboard). The app remembers your last tool, color and size.

choiceNotes.a: Ink saves as you draw. Rotation never clears it.
choiceNotes.b: Ink is not tied to screen pixels. That is exactly what keeps it in place.
choiceNotes.c: The scratchpad is a separate full-screen page for rough work.
choiceNotes.d: Strokes are stored as small vector data inside the app, not as pictures.
choiceNotes.e: Each point is stored as a fraction of the block's width and height, so the drawing follows the table.

questions.stem: You are on a plane with **no internet** and tap _Ask GPT_ on a question. What happens?

choices.text: The whole app stops working until you are back online
ChatGPT answers from a copy stored inside the app
The button is disabled with a hint; everything else keeps working
Your question is queued and sent by itself when you land
The app asks you for a paid API key

explanation.text: What Ask GPT does
It writes a short prompt (the question, the choices in the order you saw them, your answer and the app's answer) and opens `chatgpt.com/?q=…` with it. No account, no API key, no cost.

items: **Online** -> ChatGPT opens with the prompt filled in.
**Pop-up blocked** -> the prompt is copied; tap _Open ChatGPT_ in the message.
**Offline** -> the button is disabled and tells you why.

explanation.title: An outside source
explanation.text: ChatGPT is an outside source and may not match your study sources. Trust the explanation in the app first.

choiceNotes.a: The app works **100% offline** after the first visit. Only Ask GPT needs the internet.
choiceNotes.b: There is no built-in AI. Ask GPT simply opens ChatGPT.
choiceNotes.c: Ask GPT needs a connection; questions, notes and drawing do not.
choiceNotes.d: Nothing is sent in the background. You decide when to open ChatGPT.
choiceNotes.e: No keys and no costs. It is a plain link to ChatGPT.

questions.stem: You study on an iPad with a keyboard. Which key **bookmarks** the current question?

choices.text: `Space`
`Enter`

explanation.text: Keyboard shortcuts

explanation.title: First letter wins
explanation.text: **B**ookmark = `B`, **D**raw = `D`.
Striking out choices
Cross out the answers you have ruled out. Three ways do the same thing, so pick what feels natural:

items: Long-press the choice
Swipe it to the left
Tap its small **strike** button

choiceNotes.b: `M` has no shortcut. In an exam, mark a question for later with the button in the top bar.
choiceNotes.c: `S` has no shortcut. To strike out a choice, long-press it, swipe it left, or tap its small strike button.
choiceNotes.d: `Space` has no shortcut in the app.
choiceNotes.e: `Enter` presses whichever button has focus. It does not bookmark.

questions.stem: This question shows a small **Not yet reviewed** chip. What does it tell you?

choices.text: You have not answered it yet
You skipped its explanation
It is new in the latest update
Other users reported it as wrong
It was written with AI help, and a specialist has not checked it yet

explanation.text: From draft to checked

steps.text: Written with AI help, only from the owner's study sources

explanation.title: Spotted a mistake?
items: Open the **More** menu -> _Report a problem_.
Pick a reason: _Wrong answer_, _Unclear question_, _Typo or formatting_, _Explanation problem_ or _Other_.
Add a note if you like. The report is saved on your device.

explanation.text: Specialists can turn on **Reviewer mode** in _Settings_ to approve questions and export their decisions as a file.

choiceNotes.a: Your own progress shows in rings and stats, not in this chip.
choiceNotes.b: The app does not track whether you read explanations.
choiceNotes.c: New questions look like any other. The chip is about checking, not age.
choiceNotes.d: Reports stay on the device of the person who made them.
choiceNotes.e: Once a specialist approves it, the chip disappears in a later update.

questions.stem: Last week you recorded a **voice note** on a question. What is the quickest way to find it again?

choices.text: Stats -> Weak topics
Search, by saying the words aloud
Settings -> Data
Library -> Voice
Home -> Due for review

explanation.text: Everything you saved, in one place
Tap any item to open its question with the answer shown.

explanation.title: Keep your recordings safe
explanation.text: Voice notes go into a backup only when you export **with media**. The first recording asks for the microphone once; after that, recording and playback work offline.

choiceNotes.a: Stats shows your scores and weak topics, not your notes.
choiceNotes.b: Search looks through question text. Voice notes are audio, so search can't read them.
choiceNotes.d: Library has one tab for each kind of thing you save.
choiceNotes.e: _Due for review_ lists questions your schedule says are due, with or without notes.
